metadata.title: Lit3R: Retrieve-Relate-Read for Evidence-Grounded Question Answering over Scientific Literature

evidence_receipts.value: We describe tus-nlp's Lit3R (Retrieve-Relate-Read) system for LitTraceQA, a shared task for literature-grounded question answering that requires systems to retrieve relevant papers, identify supporting evidence, and generate answers. Lit3R combines off-the-shelf retrieval, reranking, and large language model (LLM) components without task-specific training. The retriever iteratively combines BM25-based sparse and dense retrieval, cross-encoder reranking, and LLM-based verification, and complements retrieval based on the question with paper-to-paper expansion. The reader first identifies supporting evidence within individual papers and then synthesizes evidence across papers to produce the final answer and evidence trace. On the official test set, our system ranked 4th on the leaderboard. Ou

findings.claim: SciRet reports hybrid BM25 plus dense recall gains in its scientific corpus, while an MS MARCO cross-encoder reduced precision in its tested setup.
Lit3R combines sparse and dense retrieval with reranking for literature-grounded QA.

note.proposed_test: On identical long-paper questions and cached passages, compare BM25, BM25+dense fusion, then fusion+reranker. Blindly assess whether answer-support spans enter the top-k and whether the fixed reader gives supported answers; measure local indexing, retrieval, and end-to-end latency.
note.question: For long papers, keep BM25 passage search or test hybrid retrieval plus reranking?

We describe tus-nlp's Lit3R (Retrieve-Relate-Read) system for LitTraceQA, a shared task for literature-grounded question answering that requires systems to retrieve relevant papers, identify supporting evidence, and generate answers. Lit3R combines off-the-shelf retrieval, reranking, and large language model (LLM) components without task-specific training. The retriever iteratively combines BM25-based sparse and dense retrieval, cross-encoder reranking, and LLM-based verification, and complements retrieval based on the question with paper-to-paper expansion. The reader first identifies supporting evidence within individual papers and then synthesizes evidence across papers to produce the final answer and evidence trace. On the official test set, our system ranked 4th on the leaderboard. Ou

uncertainties: SciRet uses CORD-19 with pseudo-relevance labels, so its retrieval scores are not a QASPER prediction. A generic cross-encoder may reduce precision in this domain; paper-specific retrieval and reranking costs are unknown.
